functions.name: Through
functions.docs:
Constructs a hyperplane passing through the two points. If the dimension of the ambient space
is greater than 2, then there isn't uniqueness, so an arbitrary choice is made.

functions.name: Through
functions.docs:
Constructs a hyperplane passing through the three points. The dimension of the ambient space
is required to be exactly 3.

functions.name: dim
functions.docs: \returns the dimension in which the plane holds

functions.name: signedDistance
functions.docs:
\returns the signed distance between the plane \c *this and a point \a p.
\sa absDistance()

functions.name: absDistance
functions.docs:
\returns the absolute distance between the plane \c *this and a point \a p.
\sa signedDistance()

functions.name: projection
functions.docs: \returns the projection of a point \a p onto the plane \c *this.

functions.name: normal
functions.docs:
\returns a constant reference to the unit normal vector of the plane, which corresponds
to the linear part of the implicit equation.

functions.name: offset
functions.docs:
\returns the distance to the origin, which is also the "constant term" of the implicit equation
\warning the vector normal is assumed to be normalized.

functions.name: coeffs
functions.docs:
\returns a constant reference to the coefficients c_i of the plane equation:
\f$ c_0*x_0 + ... + c_{d-1}*x_{d-1} + c_d = 0 \f$

functions.name: intersection
functions.docs:
\returns the intersection of *this with \a other.
\warning The ambient space must be a plane, i.e. have dimension 2, so that \c *this and \a other are lines.
\note If \a other is approximately parallel to *this, this method will return any point on *this.

functions.name: transform
functions.docs:
Applies the transformation matrix \a mat to \c *this and returns a reference to \c *this.
\param mat the Dim x Dim transformation matrix
\param traits specifies whether the matrix \a mat represents an #Isometry
or a more generic #Affine transformation. The default is #Affine.

functions.name: transform
functions.docs:
Applies the transformation \a t to \c *this and returns a reference to \c *this.
\param t the transformation of dimension Dim
\param traits specifies whether the transformation \a t represents an #Isometry
or a more generic #Affine transformation. The default is #Affine.
Other kind of transformations are not supported.

functions.name: cast
functions.docs:
\returns \c *this with scalar type casted to \a NewScalarType
Note that if \a NewScalarType is equal to the current scalar type of \c *this
then this function smartly returns a const reference to \c *this.

functions.name: isApprox
functions.docs:
\returns \c true if \c *this is approximately equal to \a other, within the precision
determined by \a prec.
\sa MatrixBase::isApprox()
